html:
The Laetoli footprints are a trail of footprints left in volcanic ash about 3.66 million years ago in northern Tanzania, uncovered by Mary Leakey's team in 1978.

Two or three upright walkers, probably of the species Australopithecus afarensis, the kind of Lucy, crossed wet ash from a nearby volcano that then hardened. The prints, about 27 metres long, show a modern arched foot and big toe in line with the others.

They proved that our ancestors walked on two legs long before their brains grew large or they made stone tools. The site is near Olduvai Gorge and is one of the most striking records of human evolution.
sum: The Laetoli footprints are a trail of footprints left in volcanic ash about 3.66 million years ago in northern Tanzania, uncovered by Mary Leakey's team in 1978.
